biblioteca_data_note: Calculated electrical response, not live audio.
biblioteca_empty: No tapes found. Try another name or tag.
biblioteca_export_error: Could not export the sheet. Try SVG format.
biblioteca_gate_note: Similarity to official presets, not hardware safety certification.
biblioteca_hardware: USB-C cable with DSP / CB5100 / 96 kHz · VID 0x3302 · PID 0x8902 · report 0xCB · WebHID · Chrome/Edge desktop · HTTPS · write-only · every write commits to flash
biblioteca_intro: Every tape holds a decision. Eleven official curves, in their original write order. Open a box and read the tracks.
biblioteca_jump_warning: The new curve may sound louder. Turn the volume down before writing.
biblioteca_listen_note: Levels matched with levelDb. The audio bar's MP3 or pink noise; browser-only volume. Listening never writes to the cable.
biblioteca_live_note: Real preview audio, after browser volume. Not cable read-back.
biblioteca_local_empty: Save the current curve to open your first local box.
biblioteca_local_error: Could not save or load the local library. Official presets remain available.
biblioteca_method_note: 601 log-spaced points, 20 Hz to 20 kHz, including preamp, without level matching. RMS and maximum absolute difference in dB. Tags: bass 20–200 Hz and treble 6–12 kHz versus mids 300–1,000 Hz, 2 dB threshold, without preamp. Balanced means below that threshold, not a flat response. Local reference, not cable read-back.
biblioteca_pack_note: S9 · reference-group curves in catalog order, preserving preamp and tracks. Kuba preset license: pending confirmation.
biblioteca_response: Calculated electrical response, 20 Hz to 20 kHz; output curve includes preamp.
biblioteca_s5_error: Name, authorship or license does not meet S5 requirements. No envelope was exported.
biblioteca_s5_license: My curve's license (I declare I hold the rights)
biblioteca_s5_note: View-only draft, not a valid S5 for publishing: no license has been assigned. Kuba presets have a license pending confirmation.
biblioteca_saved: Curve saved to the local library.
biblioteca_used: Curve loaded in the editor, without writing to the cable.
cable_confirm_connection: I will not disconnect during the write (≈0.3 s)
cable_confirm_experimental: I understand and want to write this experimental curve
cable_error_journal: The write happened, but the journal could not be saved.
cable_error_request: Could not open the cable picker.
cable_error_restore: Could not restore the cables already allowed.
cable_experimental_text: This curve uses filter types the official page never wrote. The coefficients are within the observed envelope, but the firmware has never received these formats.
cable_flash_notice: The cable memory has an unknown lifespan; memories of this kind usually withstand 10 thousand to 1 million writes.
cable_lamp_k: k · filter types and editing limits
cable_loudness_jump: Estimated difference of {delta} dB from the last curve written.
cable_loudness_unknown: The cable state is unknown: first write of the session or the last write was interrupted.
cable_loudness_warning: The new curve may sound louder. Turn the volume down before writing.
cable_queue_changed: The cable list changed. Review the queue again.
cable_queue_hint: Writes the same curve to each cable, one at a time, 2 s apart. Stops at the first error.
cable_queue_need_two: Connect at least two cables to use the queue.
cable_reason_a_b0: coefficient b0 is outside the envelope observed in the official presets.
cable_reason_a_b1: coefficient b1 is outside the envelope observed in the official presets.
cable_reason_a_b2: coefficient b2 is outside the envelope observed in the official presets.
cable_reason_a_neg_a1: coefficient −a1 is outside the envelope observed in the official presets.
cable_reason_a_neg_a2: coefficient −a2 is outside the envelope observed in the official presets.
cable_reason_b_pole_radius: poles too close to the unit circle (filter too resonant).
cable_reason_c_section_peak: this section's peak exceeds the limit.
cable_reason_d7_boost_q: Q too high for a boost.
cable_reason_d7_pk_boost_above_16k: a PK boost above 16 kHz is not allowed.
cable_reason_d_prefix_peak: the cumulative peak inside the filter chain exceeds the limit.
cable_reason_e_output_audible: the output peak in the audible range exceeds the limit.
cable_reason_e_output_full: the output peak over the full range exceeds the limit.
cable_reason_f_codec: the curve cannot be encoded in the cable format.
cable_reason_g_preamp: the preamp is outside the allowed range.
cable_reason_k_kind_not_allowed: filter type not allowed without experimental mode.
cable_refused_busy: A write is already in progress.
cable_refused_gate: The safety check refused the curve. Nothing was sent.
cable_refused_gesture: Writing needs your click on the Write button.
cable_refused_interrupted_elsewhere: Another tab closed in the middle of a write. Nothing was sent now; check the rescue notice before writing again.
cable_refused_unknown_device: The queue has a cable that is not connected.
cable_refused_unusable: The cable stopped responding during a previous write. Unplug it, plug it back in and choose it again.
cable_rescue_body: The cable state is unknown. Write Neutral or a known curve before you keep listening.
cable_rescue_note: The rescue write goes through the same checklist.
cable_rescue_reports: The cable received {count} of 9 blocks before the interruption; the final command was not sent.
cable_result_simulated: Simulated write finished. CRC {crc}. Nothing was sent to a cable.
cable_simulated_hint: This browser has no WebHID (or the page is not in a secure context). Writes are simulated and nothing is sent to a cable.
cable_status_connecting: Waiting for you to pick the cable…
cable_status_no_target: Cable connected. Choose the cable that will receive the write.
cable_target_required: No cable chosen. Choose the cable that will receive the write.
cable_write_blocked: Complete every item to enable writing.
cabo_byte_description: Header 0–13, Q23 preamp 14–17, Q27 coefficients 18–217, CRC 218–219. Wire order: b0, b2, −a1, b1, −a2.
cabo_checklist_hint: The cover opens the shared checklist. Volume, connection and experimental-type confirmations happen only there and apply to one write.
cabo_connection_error: The connection could not be completed. Try again with an explicit click.
cabo_counter_note: Counters track real attempts that reached the cable, including interruptions. Simulations and rehearsals do not increment these counters.
cabo_daily_notice: 50 or more attempts today. Consider rehearsing before the next write.
cabo_data: DATA · predicted curve level, not audio
cabo_flash_notice: The cable's memory has an unknown lifespan; memories of this type usually withstand 10 thousand to 1 million writes.
cabo_gate_note: The checklist uses the actual Q27/Q23 words. The observed envelope of the 11 official presets is not proof of hardware safety.
cabo_intro: A rack for a cable that only listens. Encode, calibrate, write. The cable never returns what it stores.
cabo_invalid: This curve cannot be encoded. Correct the parameters in the editor before continuing.
cabo_journal_empty: The journal is empty. Rehearsing the tape does not create entries.
cabo_journal_note: The cable does not return what is stored. This journal stays in this browser only. A simulation does not confirm a real cable's contents.
cabo_last_write: Latest journal entry, not read from the cable
cabo_multi_hint: Add cables with a click. To write the selection in sequence, open the checklist; the shared MultiCableQueue requests queue confirmation there, with 2 s spacing.
cabo_nominal: Report positions are nominal: 16 ms after each report, then 150 ms before commit. Individual USB report timestamps are unavailable.
cabo_power: Rack 01 · USB-C cable with DSP · encode → flash · no playback
cabo_presets: Load preset in the editor (does not write)
cabo_real: REAL CABLE · writing only after checklist and confirmation
cabo_response_description: Response calculated from the actual Q27/Q23 values, from 20 Hz to 20 kHz. Not a cable measurement.
cabo_selected_bytes: Selected report bytes, including index and zero padding
cabo_simulation: SIMULATED · no reports are sent to a real cable
cabo_spacing: At least 2 s between writes, enforced by the checklist. Never automatic; no hard cap.
cabo_support: WebHID requires desktop Chrome or Edge, HTTPS and your click. Without support, the service uses simulated cables. Connecting does not write.
cabo_timing: 9 reports · 16 ms gap · 150 ms settle · commit
cego_approximate: Approximate preview: the browser declined 96 kHz; coefficients were recalculated for the actual rate.
cego_attribution: description by Kuba · license: to be confirmed
cego_audio_error: Audio could not start. Check ♪ Audio and try pressing play again.
cego_bracket_note: The next stage compares the highest mean with two variations at half the range. Interval overlap is a conservative stopping rule, not a significance test.
cego_cable_note: Every A/B switch on the cable would rewrite the chip's flash, whose endurance is unknown. We still need to measure possible clicks. This test uses only the browser and never writes to the cable.
cego_candidates_lede: Choose 2 or 3: official presets, the current curve or variations. All pass gate v2. Names stay hidden during listening.
cego_candidates_required: Choose 2 or 3 candidates approved by the gate.
cego_chart: Means and 95% confidence intervals; complete values in the table below.
cego_ci_note: 95% CI using Student's t with n − 1 degrees of freedom, over each round's ratings. Intervals are not clipped at 0 or 10. Few rounds give wide intervals; these results describe this session, not the whole population.
cego_confirmation_required: Confirm Cable in Neutral or Other output in Setup.
cego_consent_data: I expressly consent to the future anonymous submission of the A/B pairs and ratings in the preview for community preference research, with no account or IP in the batch.
cego_consent_withdraw: I understand I will be able to withdraw consent using a local receipt. Submission and receipts will arrive in a later stage; checking these options sends no data.
cego_cost_note: Planned minimum: rounds × candidates + 1 restore. Every extra switch would cost another write. This estimate does not execute any writes.
cego_empty_results: Finish a test to see the results.
cego_engine_note: We request 96,000 Hz on the first gesture. Each section uses the Q27 coefficients and Q23 preamp the cable would use. Sound starts only when you press play, with a gentle fade-in.
cego_gate_note: The observed envelope is a policy of similarity to the official presets, not proof of hardware safety.
cego_instant: Reduced motion: positions randomized instantly. Screen closed; press play to listen.
cego_lede: Up to three curves behind the screen, level-matched and randomly ordered. Switch whenever you like; names appear only at the end.
cego_level_note: Mean gain from 300 Hz to 3 kHz, including preamp (levelDb). All candidates are attenuated to the quietest; none is boosted. Browser-only preview volume is in ♪ Audio.
cego_listen_lede: Order is randomized again each round. Numbers do not identify the same curve across rounds.
cego_meter_error: Meter unavailable in this browser. No simulated level is displayed.
cego_neutral_note: I confirm 10 × OFF + preamp −0.5 dB. The cable cannot be read: only you can confirm. This choice writes nothing.
cego_notes: Text notes (this session only, never sent)
cego_other_note: Sound card or headphones without the DSP cable in the signal path.
cego_private: Excluded from the batch: audio, filename, text notes, account data, device identifier or the curve written to the cable. These choices are not saved.
cego_random_error: A secure random order could not be generated. This browser needs crypto.getRandomValues.
cego_rating_note: Listen to every position and explicitly rate it. Zero is a valid rating.
cego_ratings_required: Listen to every position and fill in all ratings from 0 to 10 before continuing.
cego_ready: In position. Order randomized; press play to listen.
cego_scene: A treated room with three identical speakers on rails, hidden behind an acoustic screen. A tribute to Floyd Toole and Sean Olive.
cego_send_later: Sending arrives later. The button stays disabled even with consent; no network calls are made.
cego_setup_lede: The test runs only in your browser: nothing is written to the cable. Confirm your listening output before starting.
cego_share_note: Optional. Purpose: study which curves people prefer in blind listening. Proposed legal basis: explicit consent (LGPD, art. 11). No data leaves this panel.
cego_shortcuts: Shortcuts: 1, 2, 3 select a position; Space plays or pauses. Not active while editing a field.
cego_source_note: Use ♪ Audio in the top bar to choose an MP3. Without a file, pink noise plays. The same source feeds every candidate. The file stays in this browser.
cego_switch_note: Silence while switching, like in the laboratory.
cego_tied: Overlapping intervals: tie or uncertainty. Stop here; the highest mean does not prove preference.
cego_variation_note: Fixed patterns vary bass (< 250 Hz), presence (1 to 5 kHz) and treble (> 5 kHz). For a missing region, we use a free OFF slot at 150, 2,500 or 8,000 Hz. The preamp is only attenuated to pass the gate, with its value displayed. Rejected curves remain unavailable.
chrome_help_hint: Press ? to open help and Escape to close it.
chrome_language_blocked: Writing to the cable. Switch the language after the write ends.
chrome_notice: open-auri is not official or endorsed by Kuba, TTGK, Savitech or any manufacturer. Everything here was obtained by studying the protocol for interoperability purposes. Use at your own risk: we are not responsible for damage to the cable, headphones or your hearing.
chrome_soon_notice: Available as soon as the headphones reach the test bench. Until then, we do not write anything that Kuba’s original page does not write.
comparar_audio_failed: The preview or meter could not start. Check audio and try again.
comparar_bay_note: RMS for each armed pair, 20 Hz to 20 kHz, using the same level matching as Where they differ. Choose a jack to connect A and B.
comparar_blend_note: The extra head reads the base. The new layer is Δ = B − A; the result is base + k × Δ. The solver fits 10 PK/LS/OFF sections, and the gate checks the actual Q27/Q23 coefficients.
comparar_deck: Tape transport with two reels and a head block
comparar_delta: Δ = B − A · shaded regions exceed the threshold
comparar_description_credit: Kuba description · license: to be confirmed
comparar_description_original: Original Portuguese description by Kuba · license: to be confirmed
comparar_empty: Arm at least two tracks to compare.
comparar_exact: Base = A and blend 100%: exact B, for PK/LS/OFF.
comparar_export_note: Exports the Where they differ pair with names, curves, RMS, maximum and labeled regions.
comparar_failed: The operation could not be completed. Please try again.
comparar_gate_note: Envelope observed in the 11 official curves. A similarity policy, not proof of hardware safety.
comparar_gate_reason: The gate refused the coefficient or level identified by code
comparar_heads: Extra head reads the base; recording head adds the difference; playback checks the result
comparar_invalid_curve: Curve refused by the gate. The previous track was preserved.
comparar_lede: Load a curve into each track, see where two curves differ and overdub: the new curve is the base plus a fraction of the difference between A and B. Calculations use report 0xCB mathematics; the gate validates the result before any write.
comparar_match_note: 300 Hz to 3 kHz; preview attenuation only. The same matching applies to distances.
comparar_pending: Calculate the layer to check it with the gate.
comparar_rate_note: Approximate preview: the browser is not running at 96 kHz.
comparar_reason_boost: PK boost above 16 kHz or boost Q greater than 4.
comparar_reason_codec: The curve cannot be encoded in report 0xCB.
comparar_reason_preamp: Preamp must be between −25.5 and −0.5 dB.
comparar_reason_prefix: An internal peak exceeds the limit; section order matters.
comparar_reason_section: A section peak exceeds the limit.
comparar_response_note: Response including preamp · 20 Hz to 20 kHz
comparar_source_note: One source, parallel tracks. File from the Audio bar or pink noise. Browser playback only.
comparar_tracks_note: Each track holds a preset, a Library curve or a snapshot of the current curve. ARM includes it in the chart and patch bay; SOLO isolates it; MUTE hides it. Each armed track has its own live VU before the audition switch. Meters stay dark without audio.
conta_2fa_admin_note: Admin accounts only open the admin area with two-step verification on. To turn it off or set it up again, this session must have gone through the app code: if it has not, sign out and sign in again using the code.
conta_2fa_code_hint: The code changes every 30 seconds. Use the one on the screen.
conta_2fa_codes_copy_failed: Could not copy. Use the .txt file or write the codes down.
conta_2fa_codes_help: Each code works once and lets you sign in if you lose the app. They are shown only now: keep them somewhere safe before confirming.
conta_2fa_confirm_title: Confirm with a code from the app
conta_2fa_description: A 6-digit code from an authenticator app, asked for together with the password when signing in.
conta_2fa_disable_help: Turning it off leaves the account protected by the password only.
conta_2fa_error_code: Invalid code. Check that the device clock is right and type the current code.
conta_2fa_error_marker: Admin account: to change two-step verification, sign out and sign in again using the app code.
conta_2fa_error_not_enrolling: There is no setup in progress. Start again.

conta_2fa_manual_label: No camera? Type this key into the app (spaces are optional):
conta_2fa_pending_hint: If the app does not have the key yet, generate a new one: the new key and new recovery codes replace the previous ones.
conta_2fa_qr_alt: QR code with the two-step verification key, to scan with the authenticator app
conta_2fa_scan_title: Add the account to the authenticator app
conta_2fa_started: Setup started. Follow the steps below.
conta_bio_error_too_long: The bio is over the 280-character limit.
conta_bio_hint: Plain text, no formatting and no clickable links.
conta_close_ack: I understand that closing the account cannot be undone.
conta_close_always: Private data is always deleted: account, sessions, acknowledgements, drafts, favorites and activity history.
conta_close_description: Deletes your account. It cannot be undone.
conta_close_effect_anonymize: Result: account and private data deleted; public curves stay, without your name.
conta_close_effect_delete: Result: account, private data and public curves deleted.
conta_close_error_ack: Tick the box confirming that closing cannot be undone.
conta_close_error_mode: Choose what to do with your public curves.
conta_close_how: After the password, we send a link to your e-mail. The account is closed only when you open that link in this browser, while signed in, within 1 hour. You get an e-mail confirming the closure.
conta_close_mode_anonymize_help: Public curves (CC0 or CC-BY) stay on the site credited to "author removed". The nickname stays reserved for 90 days, unlinked from you, so nobody can pose as the author.
conta_close_mode_delete_help: Your public curves go offline too. People who already downloaded or wrote a copy keep it. The nickname is free at once.
conta_close_mode_legend: What to do with your public curves
conta_close_pending: Closure requested on {date}. Open the link sent to your e-mail to finish. If you changed your mind, ignore the e-mail.
conta_close_requested: We sent the confirmation link to your e-mail. The account is closed only when you open it.
conta_closed_body: Your account was closed and the data deleted according to the option you chose. We sent a confirmation to the e-mail.
conta_closed_local: The local library of this browser is not affected; to clear it, use the delete local data option in Docs.
conta_email_description: Address used to sign in and for account notices. Never shown publicly.
conta_email_error_reauth: Enter your current password to confirm the change.
conta_email_how: First we send a link to your current address, to confirm it is you. Then a link to the new address. The change happens only after both are opened.
conta_email_password_why: Your session started more than 10 minutes ago, so we ask for your password again.
conta_email_pending_body: Change requested to {email}. Open the links we e-mailed by {date}. If you do not, nothing changes.
conta_email_requested: Request recorded. Check the inbox of your current address.
conta_error_generic: That did not work. Try again.
conta_error_rate_limited: Too many attempts. Wait a little and try again.
conta_error_rate_limited_wait: Too many attempts. Try again in {seconds} s.
conta_error_turnstile: The anti-bot check failed. Solve it again and resubmit.
conta_error_unauthenticated: Your session ended. Sign in again to continue.
conta_error_unavailable: Service unavailable right now. Try again in a few minutes.
conta_error_unverified: Confirm your e-mail before doing this.

conta_export_description: Download a copy of everything we keep tied to your account, as JSON. The file is generated on the spot and is not stored on the server.

conta_lede: Public profile, security, e-mail and your data.
conta_lede_named: Signed in as {nickname}. Public profile, security, e-mail and your data.

conta_nickname_clock_now: You can change it now. After that, only in 30 days; your current nickname stays reserved for you for 90 days and redirects to the new one.
conta_nickname_clock_wait: Next change from {date}. Changing only upper and lower case is allowed at any time.
conta_nickname_error_invalid: Use 3 to 24 characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore or hyphen, starting and ending with a letter or digit.
conta_nickname_error_too_soon: You changed your nickname less than 30 days ago. Next change from {date}.
conta_nickname_error_too_soon_generic: You changed your nickname less than 30 days ago.
conta_nickname_first: Choose your public nickname. It is the only name others see on open-auri.
conta_nickname_hold_until: redirects to the current one until {date}
conta_nickname_needs_verification: Available once you confirm your e-mail.
conta_nickname_rules: {min} to {max} characters: letters, digits, dot, underscore and hyphen. Nicknames too similar to ones in use or reserved are not accepted.
conta_password_error_long: The new password is over 128 characters.
conta_password_error_mismatch: The two new passwords do not match.
conta_password_error_same: The new password is the same as the current one.
conta_password_error_short: The new password is too short.
conta_password_revoke_help: Recommended. Every other device is signed out; this one stays signed in.
conta_password_rule: At least {min} characters. A long phrase is stronger than a short password full of symbols.
conta_password_saved: Password changed. We sent a notice to your e-mail.

meta_auth_curiosity: In December 1999, his peers voted Rupert Neve the number one audio personality of the 20th century in Studio Sound magazine. He also recorded Churchill's wartime speeches for distribution to radio stations.
meta_biblioteca_curiosity: Geoff Emerick joined EMI at 16 and, at 20, took over engineering for the Beatles on Revolver (1966). He placed a microphone right against Ringo’s drums, something the studio had forbidden until then. Each tape on this shelf holds an engineering decision like that one.
meta_cabo_curiosity: Ray Dolby founded his laboratory in London in 1965 and that same year created noise reduction for tape: the signal is split into four bands and encoded before recording, and a built-in calibration tone makes sure recording and playback speak the same language. This cable only accepts the first half of the idea: it writes, but it won't let you read.
meta_comparar_curiosity: In the late 1940s, Les Paul added an extra playback head to a recorder Bing Crosby had given him: he played along with what was already on the tape and recorded everything again, layer upon layer. Years later, his eight-track recorder earned the nickname Octopus.
meta_comunidade_curiosity: Bob Clearmountain was chief engineer at the Power Station in New York and is credited with establishing the role of the mixing engineer. On 13 July 1985 he mixed Live Aid at JFK Stadium in Philadelphia: one mix for the whole world to hear at the same time.
meta_curva_curiosity: In 1966, Robert Moog applied for a patent for a filter made from a ladder of transistors (US 3,475,623, granted in 1969). In 1970, a portable instrument brought the modular's most-used connections inside the panel, without cables. The three layers of this page tell the same story.
meta_docs_curiosity: In 1928, Harry Nyquist showed that a channel of bandwidth B carries up to 2B elements per second; in 1932 he published the stability criterion that bears his name. Both ideas watch over this cable: nothing goes beyond 48 kHz, and no unstable filter is written.
meta_soe_como_x_curiosity: Before music, Andy Hildebrand interpreted seismic data for an oil company, looking for places to drill. In 1997 he released a pitch corrector that detects the note through autocorrelation and pulls the voice toward the target. Here the same idea pulls your headphones' response toward a target curve.
meta_teste_cego_curiosity: In the listening lab of an audio manufacturer, Floyd Toole and Sean Olive hid the loudspeakers behind a screen that lets sound through and hides the image; a mechanism moved each speaker into the same position in three seconds. Without seeing the brand, listeners voted on the sound. The headphone target curve was born from tests like these.
